title: Evidence, proof and reporting
status: AUTHORED. The domain that decides whether any of the rest is believed.

atom_notes.A08: evidence handling is the control over who learns what, and a report is deliberate disclosure. Everything else in this repo is worthless if this domain is weak

required_cells.why: a claim without an oracle and a control is a rumour
impact framing, or the finding is closed as informational
retest evidence, the step clients actually pay for twice
authorisation recorded before the first request

entries.name: This repo: prompts/04-prove-it.md
entries.role: The proving procedure: falsify first, control second, verdict last
preconditions: a candidate finding
oracle: one of CONFIRMED, UNCONFIRMED, REFUTED, NEEDS_ACCESS
entries.note: Local document. The rule it enforces: no CONFIRMED without a negative control.

entries.role: The adversarial review pack, the reason findings survive human review
preconditions: another agent's finding
oracle: SOUND, OVERSTATED, UNSAFE_TO_REPORT or REFUTED

entries.name: GDPR Article 33 breach notification clock
entries.role: The 72 hour clock and what starts it, which decides whether an incident is a reportable breach or a note in a ticket.
preconditions: a personal data breach has been identified
the controller is established in or targets the EU
oracle: a written record of when the controller became aware
the notification filed inside 72 hours, or a documented reason it was late
the article 33(5) register entry exists for the incident

entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry
entries.name: GDPR Article 15 and 17 request handling
entries.role: Access and erasure, tested against what the system can actually produce and delete rather than what the policy says.
preconditions: a data subject request has been received
the controller is in scope of the regulation
oracle: every store named in the request answered from, including backups and logs
erasure removes the record from each store, or the retained copy has a documented legal basis

entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry
entries.name: PCI DSS scope reduction and CDE boundary
entries.role: Whether card data enters the environment at all. Scope is the whole compliance burden, so shrinking it is the control.
preconditions: the system handles payment card data or connects to one that does
oracle: no primary account number present in a store, log or trace
the cardholder data environment boundary drawn on the network diagram matches observed flows
tokenisation used instead of a stored number on every path

entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry
entries.name: NIST Privacy Framework profiles
entries.role: A vocabulary for mapping processing purposes to controls, useful when a client needs the gap expressed in a standard both sides accept.
preconditions: the client requires a recognised framework for a privacy assessment
oracle: a current profile exists and names the functions in scope
each processing activity in the data map maps to a profile function, or is listed as unmapped

entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry
entries.name: Coordinated vulnerability disclosure process
entries.role: The reporting side of the relationship, which is also the side that decides whether a researcher is a threat or a channel.
preconditions: the organisation receives external vulnerability reports
oracle: an acknowledgement inside the stated window, measured on a real report
an embargo period stated in writing and honoured
a published disclosure after the fix, or a documented reason not to

entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry
entries.name: ISO 27001 certification scope statement
entries.role: A certificate is only meaningful against its scope. Reading the scope is the first step of relying on one.
preconditions: a supplier or the organisation claims certification
oracle: the scope statement names the system in question, not only a sibling
the certification body and the statement of applicability are available on request
the surveillance audit date is current

entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry
entries.name: Sanctions screening against a published list
entries.role: Whether a customer or counterparty can be checked against a list before service is provided.
preconditions: the service can be provided to a person or entity in a sanctioned jurisdiction
oracle: a screening result recorded at onboarding
a re-screen on the list update cadence, with the date recorded

entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry
entries.name: DOJ computer fraud charging guidance
entries.role: How the prosecution side reads unauthorised access, which is the practical boundary for what a test may do.
preconditions: a test will touch a system the tester does not own
oracle: the written scope identifies host, method and data
the scope is signed by someone with authority to grant it
third party hosting terms confirmed to permit the test

entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry
entries.name: Export control on cryptographic capability
entries.role: Whether distributing a tool with strong cryptography carries an obligation in the jurisdiction it ships to.
preconditions: the organisation distributes software containing cryptographic functions
oracle: the destination jurisdictions are listed and classified
a notification or licence exists where the classification requires one

entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry
entries.name: Legal hold overriding a deletion obligation
entries.role: When a preservation duty and an erasure duty conflict, and who decides. Systems usually implement only one of them.
preconditions: the organisation is subject to both a retention obligation and a deletion obligation
oracle: a hold flag exists that suspends deletion, and it is honoured by the deletion job
a deletion performed during a hold is detectable in the audit trail

entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry
entries.name: Statistical discipline for an oracle
entries.role: A timing claim needs a resolution, a sample size and an effect size larger than the measured noise. Without all three it is a coincidence with a graph.
preconditions: the finding depends on a measured difference rather than a state change
oracle: the noise floor measured on known negatives, reported alongside the effect
sample count and the test stated, with the separation exceeding the floor

entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry
entries.name: Reproduction package
entries.role: What a second party needs to reproduce a result without asking the finder anything. A finding that only its author can reproduce is a story.
preconditions: a finding will be handed to someone else
oracle: a second party reaches the same observation from the package alone
the environment, versions, timestamp and capture are all inside it

entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry
entries.name: ICO breach reporting path
entries.role: The regulator's own reporting route, which is what makes the deadline concrete. Reading the form is how you learn what a report has to contain before an incident.
preconditions: the organisation is subject to UK GDPR
oracle: the required fields listed and mapped to what the incident runbook collects
a dry run report completed without needing information nobody would have at hour one

entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry
entries.name: NIST Cybersecurity Framework profile
entries.role: A shared vocabulary for expressing a gap when the client needs a framework both sides accept, and a way to show that a control exists but is not measured.
preconditions: the client requires a recognised framework
oracle: a current profile naming the functions in scope
every control in the profile marked as present, measured or absent, with no blank cells

entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry
entries.name: DOJ computer crime and IP section guidance
entries.role: The prosecution side's own material on unauthorised access, which is the practical boundary a test has to stay inside.
preconditions: a test will touch a system the tester does not own
oracle: the scope document mapped against the guidance's own categories
any action that would read as exceeding authorisation, identified before the test

entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry
entries.name: EDPB guidelines on automated decision making
entries.role: What counts as a solely automated decision with legal effect, which decides whether an explanation duty exists at all.
preconditions: the system makes or informs decisions about people
oracle: each decision point classified as automated or human, with the evidence for the human step
a rationale recorded for every decision that affects a person's access or price

entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry
entries.name: Licence identification for distributed artefacts
entries.role: Whether shipping a binary triggers a source disclosure or attribution duty. A distributed artefact carries obligations the development tree does not.
preconditions: the organisation distributes software containing third party code
oracle: every dependency's licence identified against an SPDX identifier
the obligations of each licence mapped to what the distribution actually does

entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry
entries.name: Domain name dispute remedy
entries.role: What can actually be done about a lookalike domain, and how fast. A brand control that assumes takedown speed is a control with no timeline.
preconditions: a lookalike domain or impersonating site exists
oracle: the remedy route identified, with its typical timeline from published decisions
the evidence a complaint needs, collected before the domain is used against customers

entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry
entries.name: Finding anatomy: criterion, confidence, severity
entries.role: A finding has three separable parts: what was demonstrated, how sure you are, and what it would mean if true. Mixing them is how a report becomes persuasive and wrong.
preconditions: a finding is being written for someone who will act on it
oracle: the success criterion written down before the test, in the report
a confidence statement naming what could make the finding false
severity argued separately from the demonstrated fact, and labelled as inference where it is

entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry
entries.name: Scope statement and false negative disclosure
entries.role: What was not tested matters as much as what was. A reader who assumes coverage the test did not have will under-defend the rest.
preconditions: a test has finished or is being scoped
oracle: an explicit out of scope list, including paths, roles and environments
every unverified premise listed as an assumption rather than implied
the report stating what absence of a finding does and does not mean

entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry
entries.name: Minimum proof and side effect containment
entries.role: The least invasive action that still proves the claim, and what to do when the proof itself is destructive. A finding that damages the client to demonstrate itself is a second incident.
preconditions: proving the finding requires changing state
oracle: the smallest action recorded, with why a smaller one would not have sufficed
a reversal step for anything changed, or an agreed exception in writing
the stated cost of being wrong, and who accepted it

entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry
entries.name: Finding classification: sensitivity, fragility, demonstrated reach
entries.role: Three properties decide how a finding is handled: what data it touches, how unusual its preconditions are, and how far it was actually shown to reach.
preconditions: a finding is being triaged by a vendor or an internal team
oracle: the field names disclosed, classified, rather than a general claim of exposure
the configuration prerequisites listed, so the reader can tell rare from default
the demonstrated reach stated separately from the theoretical maximum

entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry
entries.name: Evidence redaction that keeps the proof
entries.role: Redaction usually removes the evidence along with the secret. The test is whether the artefact still demonstrates the mechanism after the sensitive values are gone.
preconditions: captured evidence contains credentials or personal data
oracle: the redacted artefact still reproducing the observation
each redaction marked, so a reader knows something was removed and what kind of thing

entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry
entries.name: Vendor confirmation alignment
entries.role: Whether the fix addresses the mechanism that was demonstrated or a symptom of it. A patch that closes the exact payload and not the class usually means a second report.
preconditions: a vendor has responded to a finding with a fix
oracle: the patch read against the report's mechanism, not against its payload
the original proof re-run against the fixed version, alongside the control
a bypass attempted at the class level and reported either way

entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry
entries.name: Evidence retention and chain of custody
entries.role: Whether the record of what happened would survive a challenge six months later, which needs a hash at capture, a stated handler and a retention period.
preconditions: findings may need to be defended or used in a legal process
oracle: a digest recorded at capture and re-verified later
the handler and time of each transfer recorded
the retention period stated, and the evidence still retrievable at its end

entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry
entries.name: Data handling during an engagement
entries.role: What happens to data encountered during a test. Uncontrolled copies of customer data are the most common way an authorised test becomes an unauthorised breach.
preconditions: the test will encounter production data
oracle: a written statement of what may be retained, where, and for how long
the retention actually applied, checked at close
any transfer to another system recorded and justified

tree.q: Can you reproduce this finding from what you wrote down?
tree.why: If the answer is no, nothing else in this domain matters. The test is brutal and it kills most reports.

branches.action: the finding is not ready. capture the exact request, the response, the control and the timestamp, then retry the question
branches.oracle: a reproduction that a stranger can run

next.q: Does it have a negative control?

branches.action: you have a hypothesis. run the control, or downgrade the claim
write it up: what state changed, as whom, how it persists, and what stops it
branches.oracle: report maps to CWE and SARIF

branches.action: check KEV first, then EPSS for ordering. do not use CVSS alone to prioritise

mirror.control: verbatim request and response in the report

mirror.attack: data exposure in the report itself
mirror.detect: secrets or personal data copied into the document

gaps.gap: No reporting tool enforces the presence of a negative control
gaps.build_candidate: a report generator that refuses to emit a confirmed finding without both requests

gaps.gap: No retest harness that replays the exact proving request
gaps.build_candidate: store the proving request per finding and replay it as the retest
the replay harness above, plus a diff of the oracle outcome
